title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: O(1)-memory Floyd rho in GT

claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity P in BLS12-381 G1 and an independent uniform z in GT, the attack in proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention, using at most 2^129.40 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications, C=20,000). It computes g=e(P,Q0) (a generator by nondegeneracy and prime order) and solves z=g^a by a Pollard rho on GT with FLOYD tortoise-hare cycle detection: a deterministic R-adding walk f(x)=x*M_H(x) (R=2^20) is advanced one step for a tortoise and two for a hare, both from a common start; at their meeting x_i=x_{2i} the tracked exponents give a=(A_h-A_t)/(B_t-B_h) mod r. The step count is a HARD deterministic budget of T=ceil(1.25*k0) tortoise iterations (k0=sqrt(2*r*ln(1/0.61))), each exactly 3 dense Fp12 multiplications; Floyd detects by iteration i<=rho (the rho length), so the bounded success probability is at least P(rho<=1.25*k0)=1-0.61^1.5625=0.538>=0.39 under the random-mapping heuristic (the ~1/r unsolvable meeting is a counted exceptional failure). Each multiplication is <=1.015 units (exponent updates, hashes, native adding-table loads, and the tortoise/hare element comparison). The total is W=3.75*k0*1.015=2^129.348, rounded to 2^129.40; one-time pairing/[a]Q0/encoding <=2^15.1 units. Peak memory is the 2^20-entry adding table (~2^29.3 bytes) plus O(1) walk state: far below 2^64 bytes, so a single native 64-bit address space with ordinary loads/stores suffices and NO segmented/tree/banked/distributed memory or its access cost arises. Declare memory_log2_bytes=30 (reported only; no scalar contribution). Preprocessing (table build <=2^30.3 units) is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps; generic square-root accounting, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run O(1)-memory Floyd (tortoise-hare) rho on a prime-order-l subgroup of F_q^* (cyclic, standing in for GT) for many random targets with the hard budget T=ceil(budget_factor*k0) tortoise iterations (3 multiplications each). Report the fraction of trials finding a usable collision within T -- a Monte-Carlo estimate of the bounded success probability, lower-bounded at >=0.39 in proof.md. No table beyond the adding walk, no distinguished points, no large memory. Toy-scale evidence for the random-mapping collision-time model only.
